cards.explanation: The answer is Philippi. Paul says they "…had already endured suffering and shameful treatment in Philippi." That's a rough stop to have behind you. Most folks would hit the brakes, friends, but this team kept right on going to Thessalonica.

The answer is True. Paul says that even with "strong opposition," they "…were bold in our God to speak to you the gospel of God." Notice whose boldness it is. They're bold in their God. After what happened in Philippi, that's a team that kept showing up.

The answer is God. Paul says they speak "…not in order to please men but God, who examines our hearts." Paul describes God as the One who examines hearts. So the audience that counts for this team is God.

The answer is False, and Paul says it plainly: "…we never used words of flattery or any pretext for greed. God is our witness!" No sweet talk to win anybody over, friends. What he describes instead is sharing their own lives and working night and day.

The answer is praise. Paul says, "Nor did we seek praise from you or from anyone else, although as apostles of Christ we had authority to demand it." They could have asked for a standing ovation and chose not to. I'd have had a banner made by Tuesday.

The answer is a nursing mother caring for her children. It's right in the verse: "…we were gentle among you, like a nursing mother caring for her children." Paul didn't pick a picture of power. He picked tenderness, and that tells you a lot about how this team treated people.

The answer is lives. Paul says they were "…delighted to share with you not only the gospel of God, but our own lives as well." Anybody can pass along a message, friends. Sharing your own life along with it is a whole other level.

The answer is so they wouldn't be a burden to anyone. Paul says, "We worked night and day so that we would not be a burden to anyone while we proclaimed to you the gospel of God." The text gives the reason: they didn't want to weigh anyone down. Working all day and preaching too, that's a full plate.

The answer is True. Paul says, "You are witnesses, and so is God, of how holy, righteous, and blameless our conduct was among you who believed." He's got the Thessalonians and God both vouching for them. That's a pretty solid reference list, friends.

The answer is father. Paul says, "…we treated each of you as a father treats his own children…" Back in verse 7 it was a mother, and here it's a father. Between the two, those Thessalonians were covered.

The answer is to walk in a manner worthy of God. Paul says they were "…encouraging you, comforting you, and urging you to walk in a manner worthy of God, who calls you into His own kingdom and glory." Encouraging, comforting and urging, all in one sentence. That's a team that really cared how the Thessalonians walked.

The answer is men. Paul says they "…accepted it not as the word of men, but as it truly is, the word of God…" They heard it from people, friends, and they received it as God's word. Plus Paul says it is "…now at work in you who believe."

The answer is False. Paul says it plainly: the word of God "…is also now at work in you who believe." Now, he says, not only back then. It's like a good oven, friends. It keeps working even when nobody's standing next to it.

The answer is that they suffered from their own countrymen. Paul says, "You suffered from your own countrymen the very things they suffered from the Jews…" That's how they became "…imitators of the churches of God in Judea…" The sameness was in the suffering, friends.

The answer is telling the Gentiles how they may be saved. Paul says they were "…hindering us from telling the Gentiles how they may be saved." The Gentiles are people who aren't Jews. Paul's team wanted to tell them how they may be saved.
